div.head: ECf retr 35.1d
div.ab: Quodsi expressius uolumus dicere, in quadam regione Saxonie ling ymago dicitur, adel Anglice: nobilis Latine; quod simul coniunctum sonat nobilis ymago: adeling.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 665 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

note.seg: wohl Südengland (nicht mit Coenwulf von Mercien ganz England; Birch Cart. Sax. 288), wie o. 33
probably southern England (not, as with Coenwulf of Mercia, all England; Birch, Cart. Sax. 288), as above, 33

das Suffix ist in æþeling nur -ing nicht (wie in hinderling) -ling; den Irrthum des Verfassers veranlasste vielleicht [ge]lic: similitudo oder likning: Abbild. Da Verf. damaliges hinderling (entartet, niedrig, unecht), das auch bei Orm vorkommt, aus Exeter citirt, so hörte er dort Gebürtige; es lebt noch in Devonshire.

the suffix in æþeling is only -ing, not (as in hinderling) -ling; the author’s error was perhaps caused by [ge]lic: similitudo, or likning: image. Since the author quotes the hinderling of his day (degenerate, base, spurious), which also occurs in Orm, from Exeter, he heard people born there; it still lives in Devonshire.

div.ab: But if we wish to say it more explicitly, in a certain region of Saxony ling means image, adel in English: nobilis (noble) in Latin; which joined together sounds ‘noble image’: adeling.
